note: Classification of the run on Apple M4 / macOS (seforim.db of Zayit, 7,019,636 lines, tantivy11): rows that differ are diffed line by line by tools/bench/hitdiff.py (ours-only and Otzaria-only lines, Otzaria's tag-stripping rule replayed on each); rows it does not cover keep the earlier hand classification. Applied by hitcount.py only to rows whose diff is non-zero; re-check after any engine change or other DB.
method: Every query Otzaria ran (`otz_report.py`: one word = exact, several words = advanced with the TAB distance or 1000, `w~k` = fuzzy), against ours on the positions index (tantivy11) with Otzaria-mode options: one word plain; several words `proximity: ordered, gaps = distance` and `cross_line: true` (Otzaria's advanced mode is ordered and crosses one line break); fuzzy with `ignore_quotes: true` (Otzaria's quote is transparent). Hits = matching lines. Each difference was diffed line by line (Otzaria book+segment mapped to line ids), sample lines read, and every differing line tagged by cause (scratchpad `hc_diff.py`, `hc_class.py`, `hc_fz.py`, logs `hc-*.log`).
notes: Quote-free matching (deliberate deviation, FtsLib's rule): a query word with a quote or geresh (`"`, `'`, gershayim, geresh) matches the word with the quote missing, in another place or of another kind (`ר"שי`, `רש׳י`, `רש'י`); Otzaria needs the quote of the query. Rows `large q11..q17`, `rules q11`, `rules q14` (numbers as shown): every ours-only line checked (tools/bench/hitdiff.py); with the footnote glue they account for all but a handful of lines.

Footnote marker glue, exact numbers of this run: every ours-only line of the plain single-word rows (large q2..q10, q18..q20 and the rules rows) is a line where Otzaria's `strip_html_for_indexing` glues a `<sup>` marker to the word on either side or across punctuation (`word.<sup>30</sup>` -> `word30`, `</sup><i>word` -> `5word`): 100% of the lines checked, no Otzaria-only line.

Footnote markers (most rows, ours +0.02..0.1%): Otzaria removes inline tags with no separator (`strip_html_for_indexing`; `sup` is inline), so `word<sup>5</sup>` indexes as one token `word5` and the word is lost; ours ends a word at `<sup>`/`<sub>` (FtsLib's scanner rule). Every ours-only line of the exact rows has a `<sup>` (checked all; samples 8576169, 7692606, 2451902).

Cross-line enumerators (our bug): Otzaria's `cross_line::content_range` skips a leading `(b)`, `[yg]`, `{x}` and a trailing `(49)` / `(dp"d):` when it joins two lines; ours counts them as words, so a gap is one too wide (Otzaria-only, e.g. 6175732, 6199135, 8985366) or a one-letter query word matches the enumerator (ours-only, e.g. 6172879, 6185728).

Unterminated `<` (our bug): line 5850708 has `...ayy< rbynw...` with no `>` after it; our scanner skips to the end of the line as if in a tag, so every word after it is unindexed. Otzaria keeps the `<` and indexes the rest.
Bare `&` (Otzaria bug): line 3760145 `Shiur & made ... pocket;` - Otzaria's entity rule `&[^;]+;` deletes everything up to the next `;`.

Fuzzy: Otzaria builds `FuzzyTermQuery(term, d, transposition=true)`; ours keeps FtsLib's Levenshtein (named deviation). Without `ignore_quotes` ours also misses quote words such as `wyc"xq` (quote counted as an edit), which Otzaria matches by the quote-free form.
Without `cross_line` our multi-word counts are lower by up to 39% (e.g. words q4: 87,256 vs 143,836): Otzaria's advanced mode always crosses one line break.
